Thushanthi S.
Milestone Report
Exploratory Data Analysis for Text Prediction
1. Introduction
The goal of this project is to build a predictive text model similar to those used in mobile
keyboards. This milestone report summarizes the exploratory analysis of the training data
and outlines plans for developing the prediction algorithm and Shiny application.
The main objectives at this stage are:
1. Demonstrate successful data download and loading
2. Provide basic summaries and visualizations
3. Highlight interesting findings
4. Outline next steps for building the prediction model and Shiny app
2. Data Acquisition
The dataset used is from the Coursera SwiftKey dataset.
It contains three text files in English:
en_US.blogs.txt: Blog entries
en_US.news.txt: News articles
en_US.twitter.txt: Twitter posts
All files were successfully downloaded and loaded into R using readLines().
3. Basic Data Summary
The table below shows the total number of lines, words, and average words per line for
each dataset.
Dataset Lines Words Avg. Words per Line
Blogs 899,288 37,334,690 41.5
News 1,010,242 34,372,720 34.0
Twitter 2,360,148 30,373,583 12.9
Note: Values are approximate and may vary depending on preprocessing.
4. Exploratory Analysis
We performed exploratory analysis to understand word frequency and distribution. Key
steps:
Removed punctuation, numbers, and special characters
Converted all text to lowercase
Tokenized words for frequency analysis
4.1 Histograms of Word Frequency
A histogram shows the most frequent words across the three datasets.
4.2 Word Cloud Visualization
A word cloud provides a quick overview of the most frequently used words.
4.3 N-gram Analysis
We examined bigrams and trigrams to prepare for prediction modeling.
5. Interesting Findings
Twitter data contains many short lines due to character limits.
Blogs and news data have longer text with richer vocabulary.
A few common words dominate across all datasets (e.g., the, and, to).
6. Next Steps: Prediction Algorithm & Shiny App
We plan to:
1. Create n-gram models (unigrams, bigrams, trigrams).
2. Use a backoff model or Kneser-Ney smoothing to predict the next word.
3. Develop a Shiny app where users can type text, and the app will predict the next likely
word.
7. Conclusion
This milestone demonstrates successful data loading, initial analysis, and visualization.
We are on track to build a predictive text model and an interactive Shiny app for text
prediction.
